prompt: Write the body (about 120 words) of a letter of representation from a personal injury lawyer to an auto insurer. The client was hurt in a low-speed head-on collision. Ask that all contact go through the law firm, ask for the policy limits, and ask the insurer to keep all evidence. No salutation, no signature, no names, no dates. (Internal reference C-1245; do not mention it.)
text:
We are writing to confirm that our firm now represents the injured party in connection with the collision described in your file. Please direct all further communication regarding this matter to our office and do not contact our client directly, whether by telephone, mail, or in person.

Our client was injured in a low-speed head-on collision and has been advised to undergo ongoing medical evaluation and treatment. We will provide documentation of those injuries and related expenses as the claim develops.

To allow us to evaluate the claim properly, we request a complete written statement of the bodily injury and property damage limits under each policy that may apply to this loss, including any excess or umbrella coverage. Please also confirm the name and contact details of the adjuster assigned to the file.

We further ask that your insured and your company preserve all evidence relating to the incident. This includes photographs, vehicle data and event recorder information, repair and salvage records, recorded statements, claim notes, and any dashcam or surveillance footage. Please suspend any routine deletion or disposal of such materials until this matter is resolved.

We look forward to your prompt written response.
